items.title: Efficiency and the new economics of shipping’s decarbonisation
points: Oskar Levander from Kongsberg Maritime writes for Splash today.
For almost two decades, efficiency has been routine good practice in shipping.
The EU ETS brought shipping into carbon pricing in 2024.
Member states are due to vote on adoption in December 2026.
For example, under EU ETS, every tonne of CO2 a vessel does not emit is an allowance the owner does not have to buy or surrender.
As free allocation to shipping is phased out, a container ship saving several thousand tonnes of CO2 a year avoids a large compliance cost before any fuel savings are considered.
Modelled against a conventional Kamsarmax on a similar trade, it cuts fuel use by more than 40%, and by over half on the most wind-favourable routes.
A project that looked like a seven-year payback in 2021 could instead be a three-year payback in 2026, before any premium from a greener charter rate or better finance terms is realised.

items.title: October deluge brings Panama Canal lake levels back towards normal
points: A surprisingly wet October has brought much-needed relief to the Panama Canal, with Gatun Lake recovering to near its historical average despite warnings that a powerful El Niño could trigger another prolonged drought.

New research from Ursa Shipbrokers, drawing on Panama Canal Authority data, shows Gatun Lake averaged 85.80 ft (26.15 m) over the first 30 days of October, just 0.15 ft below its historical October average.
The recovery is particularly striking compared with 2023, when severe drought crippled canal operations.
October’s average was 6.04 ft higher than the corresponding month three years ago.

Data compiled from the canal authority’s meteorological stations show 303.3 mm of rain fell across the watershed between October 1 and 29, 8.4% above the 30-year average and 83.6% more than during the same period in drought-stricken 2023.
By October 29, Gatun Lake’s daily level had reached 86.56 ft, up from an August low of 83.80 ft.

District Basic Education Officer Manish Kumar Singh said acting Principal Vijay Shankar and assistant teacher Anil Kumar were suspended late Monday night for negligence and dereliction of duty.
The process to terminate the services of shiksha mitra Deep Chandra Ram has also been initiated.

According to police, the incident took place around 9 am on Monday at the primary school in Kanaila village when 11-year-old Arshad Ahmed was sent to the school terrace to pluck bottle gourds for the mid-day meal scheme.
The boy came into contact with a high-tension wire and died, police said.
Superintendent of Police Iraj Raja said the three accused were arrested on Tuesday.

points: Maharashtra deputy chief minister and Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) chief Sunetra Pawar on Tuesday convened a meeting of party lawmakers at her official residence amid continuing speculation of friction within the party, people familiar with the matter…

The meeting comes days after a delegation of senior party officials including NCP working president Praful Patel and state ministers Chhagan Bhujbal and Hasan Mushrif, traveled to New Delhi to meet with Union home minister Amit Shah.
Neither Sunetra nor her son, Rajya Sabha member Parth Pawar attended the Delhi meeting.
Kokate also insisted that there would be no split in the party as its entire rank and file is with deputy chief minister Sunetra Pawar, who succeeded Ajit Pawar as the NCP leader, and her family.
Among the most contentious was the removal of senior leaders such as Praful Patel as national working president and Sunil Tatkare as Maharashtra state president.

items.title: Marico’s profits roar back. Can it sustain gains beyond copra windfall?
points: Marico’s investors have reason to change their mind after the September quarter (Q2FY27) earnings announced post-market hours on Monday.
Recall that the stock had slumped 9% after its Q1 results.

The turnaround in sentiment has come on the back of market-share gains and a sharp recovery in profitability, with consolidated Ebitda growing 27% year-on-year, the fastest growth in 50 quarters, as per Marico.
The Ebitda margin expanded 200 basis points (bps) to 18.2%, benefiting from softening of copra prices year-on-year.
Vietnam grew 22% and Middle East and North Africa 15%, making up for Bangladesh's subdued 5% growth amid persistent inflation and mellow demand.
Marico expects non-Bangladesh markets to account for 65% of international revenue by FY30, versus about 55% in FY26.
Gross margin expanded about 600 bps year-on-year to 48.1%, aided by copra prices falling 35% from their previous peak and a favourable product mix.

items.title: Apple Reports ‘All-Time Record’ High Revenue in India in Q4 2026 on the Back of Strong iPhone Upgrades and Mac Sales
points: Apple has revealed that the tech giant recorded its record revenue in India in Q4 2026.
Apart from India, the iPhone maker also reported strong financial performance in other emerging economies and developed markets.
Apple’s Q4 2026 revenue from iPhone sales grew by 17 percent to $57.6 billion (roughly Rs ), “despite supply and foreign exchange” challenges.
Ternus said that Apple also recorded double-digit revenue growth in the US and Greater China.
The new CEO, who took charge on September 1, attributed the all-time high financial performance to upgraders globally, including those in the US, Mainland China, and India.

This also helped the company post record-high revenue from buyers upgrading to the newer-generation iPhone models, the most recent being the iPhone 18 Pro series, which launched on September 9, along with the iPhone Duo.

items.title: MINSHIP and Oskar Wehr launch joint shipmanagement venture
points: German shipping companies MINSHIP and Oskar Wehr have launched a joint shipmanagement venture, BellRock Maritime, with an initial fleet of 12 vessels and ambitions to expand into third-party management.
The partners each hold 50% of the venture, with five ships contributed by MINSHIP and seven by Oskar Wehr.
The operation has a shore team of nearly 20 employees.
Klehr has served as managing director of Oskar Wehr alongside third-generation family boss Thomas Wehr since 2006.
He helped steer the Hamburg company through its restructuring in 2015, when Germany’s KG shipping crisis forced a substantial fleet rationalisation.
Founded in 1945, Oskar Wehr has a history of collaborating with other German owners.
In 2019, it joined Nordic Hamburg and Bertling to establish OneBulk, a commercial management platform for handysize bulk carriers.
BellRock will be led operationally by fleet director Lasse Grundmann, previously with Oskar Wehr.

Ports falling further behind shipping’s alternative fuel revolution
points: A new 65-page report from Lloyd’s Register (LR), Fuel for Thought: Ports, reveals that 1,942 alternative-fuel-capable ships were on order at the start of 2026, representing 47% of global orderbook tonnage.
The latest figures from rival class society DNV show the total number of alternative-fuelled vessels ordered in 2026 to 364, 57% higher than over the same period in 2025.
In April, South Korea’s Ulsan completed the first commercial ammonia bunkering operation, transferring approximately 600 tonnes to Exmar’s Antwerpen.

As Splash reported last month, CMB.TECH’s newcastlemax Mineral Europa took on 1,000 tonnes of green ammonia in the first commercial ship-to-ship operation involving the fuel, something that has since just been replicated in Australia with the same vessel.

Splash Ports reported in September that the International Association of Ports and Harbors fears an increasingly divided port system, with developing countries requiring between $55bn and $83bn for climate adaptation and decarbonisation.
